tag: Episode 29 · This Time, I Press It
title: This Time, I Press It

beats.t: One button filled the phone screen. Like the day Yeoni first installed the app. That day, rain had fallen, Yeoni had been angry, and a finger had slipped.
No slipping this time. Read the terms first.
Sitting on the bed, Yeoni scrolled. The text went on endlessly. A habit learned on the island that sold time. Fine print first.
[ Another Sky · The Twelve Palaces · Entry requirement: Your birth date and time ]
(Birth date and time. The Four Pillars islands didn't ask for any of this. Just sucked me in.)
One more line lay below. This sky is built from your star chart. You know best where you stand.
I know best? I barely even know my zodiac sign.
Neo sat beside the open bag. Supplies gathered overnight piled on his knees.
“You don't need that. No room.” Yeoni pointed to the thick blanket. After a moment's thought, Neo folded it in half.
“Nights could be cold. Folded in half, it fits. I'll carry it.”
Customer Support's getting a free ride. Fine, come along.
Yeoni packed things one by one. The taped umbrella. Notebook. Charger. Two red bean buns from the convenience store.
(One for me. One for her. This time, I'll carry it until she takes it.)
The talisman in the wallet grew warm again. Yeoni took it out. The crescent on the paper had half filled.
Yundal's talisman. Still warm. Use it, and it takes us to him, right?
“He said one use. Toward the guide.”
Then we find our guide first. I'm tired of wandering alone.
Yeoni tapped the birth details fields. Their fingertips trembled a little. July 6, 2002. 8:30 a.m. Seoul.
(Mom always said being born at breakfast meant I'd be lucky with food.)
[ Eulhae Yeoni · Preparing natal chart · · · ]
A twelve-part board formed on the screen. Square compartments ringed an empty center, like a game board. Tiny star names glimmered in each.
What's this? Different from the Four Pillars. Twelve spaces instead of eight characters.
“Didn't it say another sky? Another sky is read with different characters.”
More to study. My grades this semester are doomed.
Then a black spot spread in one of the twelve spaces, like a drop of ink. It slowly crept along the compartment's border.
Neo. Look. One space is turning black.
Neo set down the supplies and leaned toward the screen. His eyes hardened as he read.
“The smell of an eclipse. It's reached into that sky, too.”
She must be there, too. They dragged her into the phone.
“Probably.” Neo chose his words for a moment. “Scared? You can tell me.”
Yes. Terrified. But being scared and not going are different things.
Yeoni looked around the room. The ceiling stain. Where rain leaked. The star card on the desk. It still would not turn over.
(The first time, I was dragged away. For giving the universe one star. Not this time.)
Yeoni picked up the star card and tried lifting its corner with a nail. It did not budge. As though it were still too soon.
You're coming, too. You'll turn over someday.
They slipped it between notebook pages, then wrote in large letters on the first page.
[ Moka · Otter · Bad at rap / Yundal · Right-hand glove · Compatibility scams / Seo Hanbi · Umbrella · Uncollected: 2 / Neo · Was a cat · Human now · On my side ]
“Why write the last line?”
Even if you change again, I need to remember it's you. You've been on my side since you were a cat.
Instead of answering, Neo gently covered the back of Yeoni's hand. Gold briefly leaked between his fingers.
Okay. Rating first.
Now. I'll leave it in advance this time. I gave this app one star at first.
Yeoni opened the review field. Their finger hesitated a long time, then moved.
[ ★★★☆☆ · Being dragged away is the worst. But I made friends because of it. The other two stars after I get back. ]
“Three stars. Customer Support is moved.”
Don't be. I might deduct some when I return.
Yeoni retied their sneakers and shouldered the bag. Neo took the umbrella. Together, they stood before the door.
Ready. Customer Support, connect me.
“I'm not Customer Support.”
I know. But saying it that way makes it less scary.
The screen still held only one button. Round. With a short word on it.
[ YES ]
On that first day, the button had pulled Yeoni's finger toward it. Today, it pulled nothing. It simply waited. Leaving the choice to Yeoni.
(Nobody's forcing me to press. So this really is my choice.)
Seo Hanbi. I'm coming to get my umbrella back.
Yeoni pressed firmly with a thumb. The screen swelled white. The floor rippled like water, and the ceiling stain shone like a constellation.
Their body fell upward. Not down, up. The room shrank to a fingernail-sized square. The square became a star.
OIIINK! Wait, falling upward this time?!
“Still haven't broken the habit. Wasn't oink your pig sound?”
A habit! Habits stay even when bodies change!
Crossing the boundary, Neo's fingertips turned gold. Without thinking, Yeoni gripped his hand tightly. Their bodies did not change. Both stood in human form.
You can let go. Same this time.
I know. I'll just hold on a little longer.
Then hold tight so you don't slip.
Yes. I won't let go this time.
Their feet met ground. Stone, cold and smooth, with starlight shining up from beneath. As though another sky lay below.
Yeoni looked down at their hands. Not hooves. Five fingers. Nails. Even the watch mark at the wrist.
Human. Not a pig. I came as a human this time.
You already regained your form. What you've found once in that sky won't be lost in another.
Thank goodness. Human hands can hold an umbrella.
A vast palace stood before them. Too many roof layers to count. A star hung at every eave, swaying like a lantern.
Twelve gates punctuated the wall around it. Each had a plaque engraved with a star pattern instead of words.
[ Natal chart reading · Eulhae Yeoni · Life Palace: Yin (寅) · Main star: Lian Zhen ]
(Life Palace. Lian Zhen. I don't understand any of it.)
Neither do I. First time in this sky.
There are things you don't know, Neo?
I don't know everything. Just good at pretending.
That's an impressively honest confession.
Yeoni took the talisman from their wallet. The crescent was nearly full. The paper turned on their palm by itself, like a compass needle.
This way. Toward Yundal.
It pointed to the western of the twelve gates. Its plaque showed a horse-shaped star and a long road.
A gate of travel? Suits that con artist. Never settling anywhere.
A colonnade led toward the gate. Little star people passed between pillars, their bodies half made of light. Burdens on their backs, lanterns in their hands.
(Everyone's made of starlight. But their faces are like ours. Busy, tired.)
Yet some faces were gray, as though their light had drained away. They carried lanterns, but none were lit.
What's wrong with them? Like the gray stamps on the Island of Expression.
Eaten. Their light.
One gray-faced person stopped beside Yeoni. They looked at Yeoni—or at something beyond them.
“...The Career gate has closed. Black things come from there. Don't go.”
The Career gate? Where is that?
No answer. Carrying the lightless lantern, the star person vanished down the colonnade.
(Don't go. Why is everyone telling me not to go somewhere lately?)
There must be a reason they're warning us away. Let's find out.
Yes. That's the problem.
A sheet clung to a pillar. Wet. Even under a clear sky, water dripped from it.
Yeoni took it down. Thin, neat handwriting. Each stroke pressed carefully, like writing in a ledger.
[ Ledger · Eulhae Yeoni · Uncollected: 2 ]
Hers. Seo Hanbi passed through here.
The water smell is still strong. Not long ago.
Yeoni carefully folded the damp ledger page into the notebook, beside the star card.
I'll collect what's uncollected. So she can stop going around repaying it.
At the colonnade's end, the wind changed. Wet ash replaced the scent of stars. One side of the sky was black as spilled ink.
There. That sky looks rotten.
Step back. Not ordinary darkness.
Threads flowed from the black sky. Touching the ground, they split into fingers. The fingers scratched the stone as they crawled closer.
You came of your own accord, vessel. Nobody pushed you this time.
Yes. On my own feet. So I'll leave on my own feet, too.
Whether you leave is for this sky to decide. One of your twelve spaces is already mine.
Neo stepped forward. Golden blades from his fingertips cut three black fingers. Instead of sparks, black steam rose from the cuts.
...These hands eat Metal.
Neo, your hand! Your fingertips are black!
His right fingertips were stained as though dipped in ink. He shook his hand. The stains stayed.
Stings a little. I can still move it.
Don't say that. Every time you say that, you're not okay.
Hurting Officer rose to Yeoni's throat. They wanted to shout, to pour everything at that black sky. But they remembered Neo had been hurt every time.
(Hold it. Shout now, and Neo gets hurt again. Something besides shouting.)
Instead, Yeoni raised the talisman high. The crescent filled completely. The paper flared silver.
Silver swept the colonnade. The black fingers flinched and retreated. The talisman became ash, scattering from Yeoni's palm.
A human diviner's talisman. The Void borrows others' hands now. It won't stop me long.
The black sky slowly closed. The fingers on the ground unraveled like threads and vanished. Only wet ash remained in the air.
Silence returned. Only then did Yeoni realize they had held their breath. They let out a long sigh.
Used up the talisman. Guess the way to Yundal burned with it.
No. Look there.
Where the ash scattered, silver dust formed a line to the western gate. Like someone leaving breadcrumbs.
Not a con artist after all. Even laid out a path.
A con artist. A skilled one.
Still jealous.
Not jealousy. An objective assessment.
Yeoni looked at Neo's right hand. The stain had crept a little toward his wrist. He hid it behind his back.
Don't hide it. We agreed no hiding this time.
...I'll tell you if it spreads. I promise.
Before it spreads. That's the promise.
Neo nodded silently. Yeoni wanted to put that promise in the notebook, too.
A bell rang beyond the western gate. A very familiar voice rode the wind.
“Compatibility readings! Just your birth date and time, and I'll find your destined partner. Half price today only.”
...That voice.
Half price. It was already a scam at full price.
Suppressing a laugh, Yeoni ran toward the western gate. Silver dust shimmered beneath their feet. Behind them, a crow cawed above a distant gate marked Career.
